substitutions.why: Jacobean oak and green leather chairs, 1st class dining saloon and reception.

Louis XVI walnut fauteuils: the a la carte restaurant and the lounge. The reading and writing room and the smoke room take the wing armchairs (the leather club chair, 1.27 m deep with its footstool, does not fit the smoke room plan), so the pink fauteuil is not everywhere (#550).
Cafe Parisien, Verandah Cafes and Reception Room wicker chairs; the D deck reception rooms were furnished in wicker too (#550).
Wicker armchairs in the cafes; the D deck reception rooms were furnished in wicker too (#550).
Wicker settees in the cafes and reception room; the D deck reception rooms were furnished in wicker too (#550).
Cafe tables; the D deck reception rooms were furnished in wicker too (#550).
2nd class dining saloon swivel chairs.

1st class berths (#550).

Slatted boat-deck and promenade benches.
1st class marble-topped washstands.
2nd/3rd class and crew folding lavatories.
Electric radiant heaters (1st class cabins, crew rooms).
Upright pianos (2nd class saloon, 3rd general room).

A grand piano wherever the plan draws one (a piano footprint 1 m or more deep: the 1st class reception room). Its keyboard is the piece +X end, drawn at the plan grand's +X end, the keyboard side the piano-stool binding uses (#562).
Steel crew lockers (and crew wardrobes, drawn as lockers) in crew quarters and the crew's working rooms. Never officers' cabins, offices or sitting rooms: they keep the original kit (#1079).
3rd class wardrobes and lockers are steel lockers: 3rd class cabins, open berths and their passages (#1079).
Steel lockers in stores, machine rooms, workshops and service passages (#1079).
1st class smoking room coal fireplace (the only working one).
Reading and writing room and lounge marble chimneypieces (gaps: mj-fireplace-marble-adam).
Marconi silent room transmitter and motor-generator.
Wooden steamer chairs on the promenades.
Wooden steamer chairs on the promenades.
Carved and upholstered Victorian chairs for 1st class cabins, suites, lobbies and offices.
1st class public rooms (reading and writing room, lounges). Wicker rooms have their own planned rule.
Interim for the Jacobean oak dining saloon chairs (high carved back). Replace with mj-dining-chair-jacobean.
Interim for the 2nd class saloon swivel chairs. Replace with mj-dining-chair-2nd-swivel.
Plain wooden chairs: 2nd class library, smoke room, cabins.
The simplest wooden chair: 3rd class dining saloon and public rooms.
Crew messes, offices and officers' cabins.
Upholstered armchairs for 1st class cabins, suites and lobbies.
Wing armchairs in the smoking room and other public rooms (the tub chairs are swivel desk chairs).
Restaurant and dining saloon armchairs.
Leather club chairs: 2nd class smoking room, library and entrances.
Officers' and engineers' smoke rooms and cabins.
1st class cabin and suite sofas: Victorian carved sofas, footprint stretched to the plan, height kept.
Lounges, lobbies and public rooms.
2nd class cabin sofas and public rooms.
Leather sofas in officers' quarters.
1st class settees.
Leather settees along the walls of the 2nd class smoking room and library (stretched along the wall).
Leather settees in crew and officers' rooms.
Upholstered benches and window seats.
Small cabin stools (plan symbols about 0.36 x 0.30 m).
1st class cabin beds; footprint fitted to the plan, height kept.
Parlour suites: the big double beds.
Side, occasional and console tables against the walls of 1st class cabins, lobbies, stairs and corridors.
2nd class library and smoke room tables.
Card and occasional tables in lounges and smoking rooms.
Low occasional tables in lobbies and cabins.
2nd class public rooms.
Writing desks: reading and writing room, suites.
2nd class library writing desks.
Purser, chief steward and officers' desks.
Two-door mahogany wardrobe; footprint fitted, height 2.03 m kept. Sleeping rooms only: a bedroom wardrobe (#550).
2nd class cabin wardrobes. Sleeping rooms only: a bedroom wardrobe (#550).
Chests of drawers and bedside cabinets.
2nd class cabin chests.
Cabin dressing tables with a mirror (plan symbols about 0.80 x 0.36 m).
Suites and larger rooms: the big mirrored dressing table.
2nd class cabins.
1st class smoking room, lounge and reading room fireplaces (carved surround with overmantel). See mj-fireplace-* for period-specific ones.
Any other fireplace.
Panelled saloon bar counter, stretched along its length.
Galley, pantry and store counters: cabinet run with worktop, fitted to the plan footprint.
Serving counters and sideboards in dining and public rooms.
Serving counters and sideboards in dining and public rooms.
Cast-iron galley range; footprint stretched to the plan (long ranges look stretched; the kit range is the fallback beyond 3x).
Occasional and sofa tables in 1st class public rooms (a console table stands against a wall, not before a sofa).
Glazed mahogany bookcases in place of the plans' bookshelves of the 1st class reading, lounge and suite rooms; their own shelves are stocked (#1122).
The 2nd class library's bookcases along its walls (#1122).
An open bookcase in the captain's and officers' sitting rooms (#1122).
A glazed display cabinet of china and glass where a 1st class public room has tall shelving (#1122).
Painted cabinets and a small chest of drawers for officers' chests of drawers (#1122).

A small chest of drawers at a hospital bedside (#1122).

substitutions.why: A dressing table with a round mirror for the suites and dressing rooms (#1122); the cabins keep the vanity.
A dressing table with a round mirror in the 2nd class cabins large enough for it (#1122).
A deep upholstered sofa with a throw for the reading and writing room, the suites' sitting rooms and the private sitting rooms (#1122).
A buttoned easy chair for the private sitting rooms (#1122).
A buttoned easy chair for the captain's sitting room and the officers' and engineers' smoke rooms (#1122).
A leather settee with a travelling rug in the officers' cabins (#1122).
A low carved occasional table before the seating of the lounge, reception room and private sitting rooms (#1122).
A low open bookcase for ledgers and regulations where a crew office's shelving is low (#1122).
A small cupboard in place of a 1st class cabin's chest of drawers where it fits (#1122).
A small cupboard in place of a 2nd class cabin's chest of drawers where it fits (#1122).
